title: Arriving in Montréal at 16
text: I came to Montréal at 16, thinking French would be easy to get through,

title: Two Years in the French Welcome Class
text: but I ended up grinding it out in the French welcome class for two whole years,

title: The Secondary 5 French Requirement
text: because here your French has to reach the level for your age before you can move on — like me, I was 17 at the time, so my French had to be at Secondary 5 level,

title: Only “Bonjour” and “Merci”
text: and for someone like me, who had never studied French and arrived knowing only “bonjour” and “merci”, it was just too hard.

title: Switching to Adult High School
text: So I transferred to an adult high school and finished all my courses there.

title: A Winter Finish, Few Programs Open
text: Because I finished my courses in winter, there weren't many programs I could apply to at the time.

title: Choosing International Business
text: I figured, since I'm here anyway, I might as well go for it — so I chose International Business.

title: Acing the Language Courses
text: It turned out I did really well in my college language courses,

title: Swamped by Finance and Western History
text: but the finance courses in my program and Western history left me completely overwhelmed.

title: Failing History in the First Semester
text: In my first semester I failed history, no surprise. I barely passed my program courses.

title: A Friend Met Through Dota
text: Around then, because I loved playing Dota, I met a good friend online who had just done a year of computer science.

title: Switching to Computer Science
text: He recommended I study computer science. So I switched over, just like that,

title: Graduating and Joining Lowkler
text: learned lots of different languages, both front end and back end, and graduated without a hitch. Then a friend referred me to a job at Lowkler.

title: Launching React for the First Time
text: There, I learned for the first time how to start up a React app.

title: Learning the Team Toolkit
text: I learned Slack, how to use GitHub, how to work in Agile cycles, and how to assign tasks in Trello.

title: An E-commerce Site Without Middlemen
text: There I built an e-commerce website: a supply site that cut out the middlemen and connected warehouses directly with web users,

title: Internship Over, Back to ÉTS
text: but then the internship came to an end. Afterwards I went back to taking classes at ÉTS, while looking for every kind of job opportunity,

title: Full Stack Developer at Orispark
text: and later landed a role as a Full Stack Developer. Orispark — Remote | Jul 2024 – Jan 2025

title: A Management System for Tsinghua Wuxi
text: Contributed to an internal management system for Tsinghua Wuxi Research Institute, a state-owned institutional project, translating URS documents and client UI designs into production-ready frontend modules.

title: React & TypeScript Pages
text: Independently developed React and TypeScript pages with Redux, Material UI, custom components, and SVG-based layouts, improving visual consistency across internal management workflows.

title: Connecting Frontend and Backend
text: Integrated frontend modules with a Python MVC backend through Axios to retrieve database records, submit form data, handle validation errors, and keep displayed business data synchronized.

title: Reusable Data Management Components
text: Built reusable forms, record tables, filters, and detail views for internal data management, reducing repetitive page-level implementation and making future module delivery faster.

title: Working with Product and Backend Teams
text: Worked with product and backend teams to confirm API contracts, field mappings, and client feedback updates, reducing integration issues during testing cycles.

title: AI Rises, Jobs Shrink
text: After that, I kept studying at ÉTS. With the rise of AI, there were fewer and fewer jobs, so I decided to keep sending out résumés while building fun things with AI.

title: PartnerHub, Inspired by Daily Job Hunting
text: During this time I built PartnerHub (I was on LinkedIn and Indeed every day looking for work, so I made something with similar features — when you use something every day, how could you not get used to it?)

title: SmartDépanneur, for Mom's Store
text: and SmartDépanneur (my mom runs a store, so I wanted to help her out).

title: A Trilingual Property Platform
text: A friend of my mom's who works as a real estate broker asked me to build a property listing site: Propriété En Vente — Trilingual Québec Property Platform.

title: Still Looking for the Next Role
text: Right now, I'm still looking for job opportunities.
